types.name: Native public
types.summary: Public coins, like NIGHT. The contract mints them and steps out: they move wallet to wallet with no contract involved, and anyone can see who holds how much.
types.private: Nothing. Holder, amount and every transfer are public.
types.nft: A serial-numbered domain minted once with a supply of 1, so its token type is one of a kind.
types.burn: Natively: send the coins to the all-zero address.

types.name: Native private
types.summary: Private coins in Midnight's Zswap pool. Once minted they move peer to peer, and nobody can see the amounts or who holds them.
types.private: Holders, recipients and amounts after minting. Mint amounts are public.
types.nft: The same serial-derived domain, minted once with a value of 1.
types.burn: Through the contract, to the shielded burn address, counted in its supply.

types.name: Contract public
types.summary: Balances kept in the contract's own public state, like an ERC-20. Its four conversions turn a balance into either kind of coin and back.
types.private: Nothing: balances are public, keyed by a hash of each holder's secret.
types.nft: Serial-derived domains held in the balance map with a supply of 1, which convert like any other.
types.burn: Not included; supply is minted, moved and converted.

types.name: Contract private
types.summary: Balances the contract keeps confidential, as notes: commitments in a Merkle tree, spent by revealing a nullifier. A transfer shows no token, no amount and no parties.
types.private: Everything about a transfer. Conversions to coins reveal the token and amount, because coins need them.
types.nft: A note of amount 1 under a serial-derived domain, moved as privately as any other.
types.burn: Not included; notes convert to coins, which can be burned.

questions.q: Can all four types hold both fungible and non-fungible supplies?
questions.a: Yes, all four here do, and each has minted both on preview. For the two native types an NFT is a token type of its own with a supply of 1. For the two contract types it is an entry in the contract's books with a supply of 1. MIP-0004 itself covers only fungible tokens; the NFT side of our contract token follows the same conversion rules, and is our extension.

questions.q: Can a token move from a shielded address to an unshielded one?
questions.a: Not by itself. Shielded and unshielded tokens are different token types in separate pools, and the ledger has no primitive that converts one into the other. A contract can do it for its own tokens: MIP-0004's unshield takes a private coin into the contract's balance, and toUtxo pays that balance out as a public coin of the same asset. We ran both on preview.

questions.q: Can a token move from an unshielded address to a shielded one?
questions.a: The same way in reverse: fromUtxo takes public coins into the balance, and shield pays them out as a private coin. Our private (kind 3) contract has the same four conversions, so an asset can go from a public coin into hidden notes and out as a private coin.

mips.title: Native unshielded token
mips.note: Family profile: one contract, many token types. Minting is restricted to the issuer with a hash-based secret, never ownPublicKey(). name, symbol, decimals, tokenColor and the mint counter are all there.

mips.title: Native shielded token
mips.note: Family profile with the supply and derived-nonce extensions. We put the issuer's secret inside the derived nonce, so a recipient cannot be found by trying known keys; MIP-0011's own version is recipient-public.

mips.title: Contract token with UTXO conversion
mips.note: All four conversions, supply-neutral, on chain. Accounts are hash-based rather than ownPublicKey(), which would let anyone move another account's balance to themselves through toUtxo. totalSupply and balanceOf are public state rather than circuits: with them the contract was too large to deploy on preview.

mips.title: Public contract log emission
mips.note: emit needs Compact 0.33 or later, which targets ledger 9. Preview, preprod and mainnet run ledger 8, where emit does not compile. Events go to contract state instead, in MIP-0002's standard event types; the preview indexer already has the contractEvents query waiting.

mips.title: On-chain token metadata
mips.note: The same 256-byte TokenMetadataPayload, the same kind byte and validation rules, last write wins per key. Stored in contract state and logged as a Misc event, because the event transport needs ledger 9.

agents.title: Spending caps
agents.body: NIGHT an agent may pay without asking, per payment and per day.

agents.title: Whitelisted contracts
agents.body: The only contracts an agent may call. Anything else is refused before it reaches the operator.

agents.title: Blocked addresses
agents.body: The operator's list and each agent's own. Public addresses are also blocked in the treasury contract.

agents.title: Sessions
agents.body: Tokens that expire, each with its own budget of requests and NIGHT, revocable at any time.

agents.title: Private caps per draw
agents.body: Each mandate commits to its agent's cap. A draw proves it is under the cap without revealing the cap or the agent.

agents.title: Draws per period
agents.body: Each agent has a number of draw slots per period, each with its own unlinkable nullifier.
